title: Mint and Coriander Green Chutney
summary: A vivid, fresh green chutney of mint and coriander blended with chilli, ginger, toasted cumin and lemon, ready in ten minutes.
equipment: high-speed blender or small food processor

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast the cumin
steps.text: Toast the cumin seeds in the dry pan over a medium heat for about 1 minute, shaking, until they smell nutty. Toasting brings out the oils and gives the chutney a warm backbone.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Put the cumin, mint, coriander, chilli, garlic, ginger, lemon juice, sugar, salt and 60 ml of the water in the blender. Blend 30-60 seconds, stopping to scrape down the sides, until completely smooth.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.text: Add the rest of the water a spoonful at a time until the chutney is thick enough to coat a spoon. Taste and add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lemon if needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon into a bowl and serve with samosas, pakoras, grilled meats or sandwiches. The lemon juice helps keep the bright green colour.

tips: Make sure the herbs are completely dry after washing, or the chutney will be watery.
The usual mistake is adding all the water at once; blend with a little and loosen gradually.
For a creamy version to serve with kebabs, stir 2 tbsp into 150 g plain yoghurt (adds milk).
Pull mint leaves off their tough stems, but tender coriander stems add flavour and can go in.
storage: Refrigerate in a covered jar with a thin film of lemon juice on top for up to 3 days. Freeze in ice-cube trays for up to 3 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
